rationale: 2 major findings block: ChatHeader.tsx's truthy check hides a legitimate $0.0000 classifier cost row, and chatGeneration.ts's `??` routing merge cannot apply an explicit `routing: null` clear from the backend (reachability unconfirmed from the frontend alone, and tracing it pushed this round past its 24-call budget). Two other edge-case reports in CredentialFields.tsx (function-typed label bypass; textarea/select branches ignoring an explicit label) were traced to every current config producer in the repo and found genuinely unreachable today, so they were dismissed rather than deferred (0 deferred, 5 dismissed as noise/unreachable). Acceptance lens confirms all 4 SharePoint field-order/label/shared-config/regression-test criteria pass; standards review was not expected for the compact profile (na, no coverage gap).

findings.title: Classifier cost row hidden when cost is exactly zero
findings.problem: `if (classifierCost)` treats a real `total_classifier_cost_usd` of exactly 0 as falsy, so the 'Classifier cost' row is omitted from the usage-details overlay — indistinguishable from the classifier never having run.
findings.impact: A user cannot tell 'classifier ran and cost $0' from 'classifier did not run'; the sibling 'Money spent (approx)' row in the same render always shows via `?? '0'`, so the two rows behave inconsistently for the same zero-value edge case.
findings.recommendation: Use a definedness check instead of a truthy check, e.g. `if (classifierCost !== undefined)`.

findings.title: Routing merge cannot apply an explicit null clear
findings.problem: `existingThought.routing = thought.routing ?? existingThought.routing` uses nullish coalescing, so a streamed chunk that explicitly sends `routing: null` to clear a prior routing assignment is swallowed and the stale value is kept. `Thought.routing`/`ThoughtBackend.routing` are the only fields in this merge typed `| null` (every sibling field here is a plain optional), a concrete signal that an explicit clear was anticipated by the type but not implemented in the merge.
findings.impact: If the backend ever sends an explicit `routing: null` to retract a routing assignment mid-stream, the UI keeps showing the stale routed-model label for that thought indefinitely.
findings.recommendation: Distinguish 'absent' from 'explicitly null' with an `in` check, e.g. `existingThought.routing = 'routing' in thought ? thought.routing : existingThought.routing`.
